features.description: `dontpanic capabilities status` CLI + local cache + `ProbeStatus.PENDING`. New subcommand `dontpanic capabilities status [<id>] [--format=text|json] [--profile=<name>] [--no-cache-write]`. Reads manifests via the existing F001 loader (from V0a plan 2026-05-21-001 — already shipped), executes declared probes (using probe `capability_id` binding from V0a F002 where present; degrades gracefully when probes lack capability_id binding by treating unbound probes as informational). Adds `ProbeStatus.PENDING` enum value with semantics `needs_probe_implementation / unknown` — distinct from PASS/FAIL/WARN/ADVISORY and explicitly NOT a synonym for `blocked`. Per-capability status is computed from the CLOSED set `{ready, needs_setup, blocked, not_installed, optional}` — `pending` is NEVER a capability status (PENDING is a probe-state only). Output formats: text (table with ✓/✗/… badges, owner_boundary chip, configured/missing/next-actions lists) and JSON (stable agent-handoff shape with `automatable[]` + `human_required[]` arrays derived from `setup_steps[]`). Writes `~/.dontpanic/capabilities-status.json` cache on every run unless `--no-cache-write`. `--profile=<name>` filters to capabilities whose `default_in_profiles` contains <name> or that are required by manifests in the profile.
steps: Add argparse subparser: `dontpanic capabilities status [<id>] [--format=text|json] [--profile=<name>] [--no-cache-write]`. Subcommand lives in a new sibling module `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities_status.py` (NOT a `capabilities/` package — would collide with the existing `capabilities.py` module).

Add `ProbeStatus.PENDING` enum value to the existing ProbeStatus type. Define semantics in code docstring + this plan's evidence: `PENDING = needs_probe_implementation / unknown — NOT a blocker; capability containing only PENDING probes can still be 'ready' if its requires resolve`.

Implement compute_capability_status(manifest, probe_results, requires_resolution) -> CapabilityStatus enum returning one of {ready, needs_setup, blocked, not_installed, optional}. Rule: `not_installed` if capability requires an adapter and no adapter registered. `optional` if not in any active profile. `blocked` if any non-PENDING probe FAILS. `needs_setup` if any `requires.{env,auth,files,config}` entry unresolved OR any non-PENDING probe WARNs. `ready` if all non-PENDING probes pass AND all requires resolve. PENDING probes alone NEVER produce `blocked`.

Implement text renderer: per-capability section with status badge + owner_boundary chips (core/adapter/operator), Configured list (resolved requires), Missing list (unresolved env/auth/files/config), Next actions list rendered from setup_steps[] (entries with automatable=true labeled `[automatable]`, automatable=false labeled `[human-required: <human_required_reason>]`). PENDING probes render as informational chip below the status badge: `probe pending: <probe_name> — <reason>`.

Implement JSON renderer: stable shape `{schema_version: '1.0.0', generated_at: ISO8601, capabilities: [{capability_id, status, owner_boundary, configured[], missing[], automatable[], human_required[], pending_probes[], next_actions[]}]}`. Document shape in `evidence/json-schema-doc.md`. Snapshot test pins shape.

Implement cache writer: `~/.dontpanic/capabilities-status.json` written after every status run unless --no-cache-write. Content identical to --format=json output. Cache file mode 0600 (operator-only).

Graceful degradation: if no probes have capability_id binding (V0a F002 not yet shipped), all capabilities still get computed status using requires-resolution alone + a single advisory note explaining the binding gap. Do NOT block on V0a F002 completion.

Add fixture tests test_capabilities_status_cli_f002.py: ≥10 cases covering all-ready, mixed-status (firebase-dashboard needs_setup + claude-cli ready), single-capability detail view (`status firebase-dashboard`), JSON shape stability via snapshot, profile filter, cache write, --no-cache-write flag, PENDING probe does NOT cause blocked status, PENDING probe renders as informational chip, automatable/human_required partition derives correctly from setup_steps, unknown capability_id positional arg exits non-zero with closest-match suggestion.
Run full orchestrator sweep + sanitization.

features.description: Plan-lock advisory required-capabilities sidecar. Add an OPTIONAL `requires_capabilities[]` array to the existing `claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/plan.schema.json` (additive — backward-compat for plans without it; absent or empty array = no advisory). `dontpanic plan lock` reads both `external_refs[]` (v1.10.0 substrate from plan 2026-05-20-001 F002, ALREADY landed in plan.schema.json with `kind`/`uri`/`sync` enum) AND the new `requires_capabilities[]`, validates each capability_id against the manifest registry (F001 loader), and emits `evidence/required-capabilities.json` summarizing per-capability readiness (sourced from the F002 capabilities-status cache or recomputed if cache absent). Lock output displays a warning chip when any required capability has status != `ready`. **Sidecar is advisory only — lock proceeds even when capabilities are not ready.** Unknown capability_id in `requires_capabilities[]` fails lock loud with closest-match suggestion (this IS a hard error — operator-introduced bad reference, not an environment state issue). This F003 depends MORE strictly on V0a F002+F003 substrate than F002 does because the sidecar binds capabilities to plans, which is the natural seam where probe + adapter capability_id binding pays off.
steps: Add optional `requires_capabilities[]` field to claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/plan.schema.json. Items: string matching capability id pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`. uniqueItems. NOT added to the schema's required array — additive only.
Bump agent-conventions VERSION minor again (or fold into F001's bump if delivered together) with changelog note.

Implement scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities_lock_sidecar.py: `emit_required_capabilities(plan_dir: Path, *, status_cache: Path | None = None) -> Path | None`. Reads plan frontmatter, extracts external_refs[] capability bindings (where the URI scheme maps to a registered adapter with capability_id) + requires_capabilities[], queries CapabilitiesStatus (F002 cache if present, else recomputes via load_capabilities + run_probes), writes evidence/required-capabilities.json with {plan_id, generated_at, required_capabilities: [{capability_id, status, missing[], next_actions[], owner_boundary, source: 'external_refs' | 'requires_capabilities'}]}. Returns Path to sidecar or None if plan has neither external_refs nor requires_capabilities.

Wire dontpanic plan lock CLI to call emit_required_capabilities after status flip. Validate each capability_id in requires_capabilities[] against the manifest registry BEFORE emitting sidecar; unknown id fails lock loud with closest-match suggestion.
Lock output displays warning chip when any required capability has status != ready: `WARN: plan requires N capabilities not ready (see required-capabilities.json)`. Lock proceeds regardless.

Sanitization: required-capabilities.json must NOT contain command_template strings from setup_steps (avoid leaking placeholder examples that look like secrets). Sidecar emits next_actions as human-readable summaries (`step.what` field), not raw commands.

Add fixture tests test_plan_lock_required_capabilities_f003.py: ≥8 cases including: (a) no external_refs and no requires_capabilities → no sidecar emitted, no warning. (b) requires_capabilities with ready capability → sidecar emitted, no warning. (c) requires_capabilities with not-ready capability → sidecar emitted, warning chip displayed, lock proceeds. (d) external_refs[].uri resolves to a registered adapter with capability_id → that capability_id pulled into sidecar with source='external_refs'. (e) Unknown capability_id in requires_capabilities → lock fails loud with closest-match suggestion. (f) Status cache absent → sidecar recomputes status. (g) Status cache present → sidecar reads from cache. (h) Plan with only external_refs whose URI doesn't map to a known adapter → sidecar emits empty required_capabilities array + advisory note.
Run full orchestrator sweep + sanitization.
